For the God who, by His power, settled water in the earth, can by His power also take it away. It is Allah's grace and bounty that He has kept it in place.

These two examples are those that were deeply rooted in people's minds in that era, while all other kinds of fruits and animals also came into being from water.

Among all the other produce, the olive tree has been mentioned specifically.

It is near that sacred valley where Musa (peace be upon him) was granted prophethood. Therefore it has been mentioned specifically. This tree too grows there because of the water that is preserved within the earth.

Now, after plants, a look at the world of animals.

Lesson 149: Explanation of Verses 23 to 52

The theme of this lesson moves directly from the evidences in the self and the horizons to the doctrine of Tawhid (the Oneness of God), which has been the central axis of the call of all the Prophets, and to which all the Messengers have invited. It is explained that all the Messengers, in all ages, called people to this same belief, and how their nations received each Messenger. What was their response to this call? Thus, from Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) until today, all the Messengers gave the call to the word of Tawhid, whose meaning in Arabic is: "For you there is no ilah (deity) except Allah," because all the Messengers gave their call in the language of their own people. Thus Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) also said the same thing that the Prophets after him said to their nations, and all the nations gave one and the same answer, even though between these nations there were long distances of time and place.

Wa-laqad arsalna Nuhan (verses 23 to 25)

﴿Bi-qawmi u'budu Allaha ma lakum min ilahin ghayruh﴾ (23:23): "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him." This is the word which is the call of all the Messengers, and it does not change. This entire universe stands upon this word. This entire universe for it...

﴿Afala tattaqun﴾ (23:23): "Will you not fear?" That is, do you not fear the evil end of the denial you make concerning this great truth? Whereas all other realities are a consequence of this truth, and your denial is an assault upon this great truth, and a people who deny this truth necessarily become deserving of a great punishment.

But concerning Prophet Nuh you say... Whereas all other realities are its consequence, and your denial is an assault upon this great truth, and a people who deny this truth necessarily become deserving of a great punishment.

But the great and influential people of the people of Prophet Nuh do not express doubt about the truth of this word, nor do they demand any proof concerning this word, nor do they reflect upon it. In reality they are caught in the narrowness of their own personalities, and they cannot free themselves from it. Their thinking is confined to the personality of the caller. They do not have the ability to rise above this limited thinking and reflect upon this great truth which Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) presents. Thus, instead of saying anything about the principled and great call of Prophet Nuh, they began to comment upon the personality of Prophet Nuh, whereas this entire universe is witness to the ideology and call of Prophet Nuh, and what matters is what a person says, not who says it.

﴿Fa-qala al-mala'u alladhina kafaru min qawmihi ma hadha illa basharun mithlukum yuridu an yatafadhdhala 'alaykum﴾ (23:24): "The chiefs of those among his people who disbelieved said: 'This is none but a human being like you, who wants to make himself superior over you.'" The people of Prophet Nuh viewed his matter and this great call with extreme narrow-mindedness and shortsightedness. Because of this narrow-mindedness and shortsightedness they were not even capable of understanding the reality of this call or grasping its consequences. Their esteemed and false personalities kept the reality of this call and its essence hidden from their sight. They remained blind, and because of this blindness, veils came between them and this call. Their viewpoint could not get out of the circle of the personality of the caller. They could only understand this: if we accept this call, then an ordinary person like Nuh will become a great person. Obviously, as soon as we believe, he will become our leader and a great man.

Because of their narrow-mindedness, these people thought that Prophet Nuh was working only for his own personality, and that is why he claimed prophethood. But because of this shortsightedness, they not only deny the excellence of Prophet Nuh, but in reality they also deny a great excellence granted to humanity. Allah the Exalted had given this honour to the human species because He created it as a thinking creature. The thinking of these people was that if Allah were to send someone as a prophet, that person would necessarily have to be from among the angels. In effect, these people wanted to deprive humanity of this honour.

﴿Wa-law sha'a Allahu la-anzala malaikatan﴾ (23:24): "Had Allah wished to send a messenger, He would have sent down angels." They say this because the power that would connect their souls with the higher world does not exist in them, so that they could believe that chosen individuals among humans can receive bounty from the higher world, guide their other brothers, and connect them to Allah.

These people now think about this important matter in the light of the ideas inherited from their forefathers.

﴿Ma sami'na bihadha fi aba'inal-awwalin﴾ (23:24): "We never heard of this among our forefathers of old." When imitation extinguishes the heart and vision of a person, just as a fire goes out, and when human thinking gives up its work, people stop thinking about the problems confronting humanity. If they do not find something in their jahili traditions, they refuse even to accept it. These people only look backward.

This is the conduct of these stagnant and extinguished societies, and this is their thinking: that what has happened once can happen again, and what has never happened cannot happen. In this way stagnation comes into their lives. Life does not remain dynamic, and people become confined to the narrow circle of those actions which their forefathers once performed.

Would that people of this kind could realize that they are stagnant and imitative, and yet they criticize those who call to freedom of thought, who say that the evidences in the existence of the universe should be reflected upon for faith. But these people respond to this call to freedom of thought with ridicule and accusations.

﴿In huwa illa rajulun bihi jinnatun fa-tarabbasu bihi hatta hin﴾ (23:25): "He is nothing but a man possessed by madness, so wait with him for a while." That is, wait a time, meaning: let him die, and you will be rid of him, and of his call, and you will no longer need to answer his call.

The denial of these people reaches such a point that Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) finds no way to reach their hearts with the Islamic call, and no place of refuge from their mockery and persecution. Now he turns only towards his Lord; he seeks help from his Lord in his difficulties.

Qal rabbi-nsurni bima kadhdhabun (26)

When living human beings adopt such a stone-like stagnation, when life stops moving forward and people abandon the stages of progress and perfection that Allah has set for mankind, such people become obstacles in the path of human advancement. Then there are only two possibilities: either life is left frozen in that place, or those who have stopped the cart of life from moving forward are shattered to pieces. Concerning the people of Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him), this very decision was made: that they should be removed from the path of humanity. For the time of Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) marks the beginning of the era of humanity. Therefore Allah threw that heavy stone aside from the path of humanity.

**Verse 27 (Surah Al-Mu'minun, 23:27)**

Thus the Divine Sunnah (the established way of Allah) removed this obstacle from the path of human life's growth and development, the obstacle of the people of Noah. This was so that human life could advance along the highway of progress. In the time of Hadrat Noah (peace be upon him), the growth of humanity had begun, and at its very beginning stagnation and inertia had appeared in it. This is like a delicate plant that, as soon as it emerges from the earth, faces heavenly calamities or other difficulties, so that it wilts and dries up, since it is weak. To remove these difficulties, the flood was the best remedy. It should be remembered that a flood washes the earth clean, and after a flood the earth produces a harvest. In the same way, the earth was purified of the filth of the people of Noah, so that correct human life could begin afresh on this globe and human life could proceed well and smoothly along the highway of progress.

﴿So We revealed to him, "Build the ship under Our watchful eye and according to Our revelation."﴾ (23:27). This ship was the means of salvation from the flood, and it was also the means by which those who had believed would be saved, so that the continuation of the human race would be assured, just as a seed is preserved and then sown. It was Allah's will that Hadrat Noah should build this ship with his own hands. In this there was a lesson: that human beings must live on this earth according to the means and resources available, and that every person must strive wholeheartedly to earn a living, so that they become deserving of help from their Lord. Allah's help is given only to those who strive tirelessly, not to those who remain immersed in luxury and comfort and live a life of ease, nor to those who merely wait for others and make no effort for anything else. Allah's plan for Hadrat Noah was that he would become the second Adam of humanity. Therefore he was taught that he must himself adopt the means and resources for his life. Allah's watchfulness would remain with him, and Allah was indeed teaching him to adopt means. He was to build this ship so that through it Allah's will might be fulfilled. For the beginning of this process of cleansing the globe, Allah had appointed a sign for Noah.

﴿Then when Our command comes and the oven overflows...﴾ (23:27). That is, when water gushes forth from the oven, this will be the sign of the coming of the flood, and then it will be Hadrat Noah's duty to board the ship quickly and take with him on the ship a pair of the seed of life.

﴿...then load into it a pair of every kind, two of each...﴾ (23:27). That is, all animals and all birds, and plants and the like, those known to humans at that time and from which the human race benefited.

﴿...and take your family aboard, except those against whom the word has already gone forth...﴾ (23:27). This decision concerned those who had disbelieved and denied Hadrat Noah. A decision had already been made that they would be destroyed, because they had denied Allah's signs, and it is Allah's Sunnah that deniers are destroyed.

Hadrat Noah (peace be upon him) was given the final command that he should no longer argue or dispute with these people, nor try to save any of them, even if one of them was a close relative, because Allah had decided the destruction of all the disbelievers.

﴿...and do not address Me concerning those who have done wrong; indeed, they are to be drowned.﴾ (23:27). This is because Allah's Sunnah does not make exceptions for a friend or a relative. Its path is perfectly straight, and there is no crookedness in it.

What happened after this is not detailed here, because it has already been said that they are all to be drowned. Now Hadrat Noah is told how he should express gratitude for Allah's blessings, how he should recite Allah's praise, and how he should seek guidance from Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah al-Mu'minun (23), verses 28–29:

"Then say: 'All praise is for Allah, who has delivered us from the wrongdoing people.' And say: 'My Lord, cause me to land at a blessed landing place, and You are the best of those who bring to land.'"

In this way you should praise Allah, turn your attention towards Allah, describe the attributes of Allah, and learn and teach the acknowledgment of the signs (of Allah). This is the teaching of Allah for His servants. Allah first teaches the Prophets, and they then teach the common people, and these Prophets always become an example for the common people.

"Then say: 'All praise is for Allah, who has delivered us from the wrongdoing people.' And say: 'My Lord, cause me to land at a blessed landing place, and You are the best of those who bring to land.'"

In this way you should praise Allah, turn your attention towards Allah, describe the attributes of Allah, and learn and teach the acknowledgment of the signs (of Allah). This is the teaching of Allah for His servants. Allah first teaches the Prophets, and they then teach the common people, and these Prophets always become an example for the common people.

The passage begins with a fragment of the verse ("Indeed, [in this] are signs; and indeed We were ever testing [mankind]") and the text as given.

"Indeed ... those who are tested (verse number)." There are many kinds of trials at the outset: some trials are for patience (sabr), some trials are for gratitude (shukr), and some trials are for reward (ajr). In the story of Noah there is every kind of trial and a lesson for those who come after.

Now comes the scene of another messenger, and the consequences of denial, since the call is also one and the messengership is also given.

Thumma anshanaa ... lilqawmi-z-zalimeen (verses 31 to 41)

Although the language of Hadrat Nuh was different and the language of the messenger under discussion was different, because between these two messengers there was a difference of centuries (qurun).

What was the answer of this people? It was the same answer, namely denial: Wa qaal al-mala'u min qawmihi alladheena kafaroo wa kaddhaboo bi-liqaa'il-aakhirati wa atrafnaahum fil-hayaatid-dunyaa ma haazaa illaa basharun mithlukum ya'kulu mimmaa ta'kuloona minhu wa yashrabu mimmaa tashraboon (23:33), wa la-in ata'tum basharan mithlakum innakum idhan la-khaasiroon (23:34): "The chiefs of his people who disbelieved and denied the meeting of the Hereafter, and whom We had given ease in the life of this world, said: This man is nothing but a human being like you; he eats of what you eat and drinks of what you drink. This is the same objection that every nation raised: that this messenger is merely a human being like you. This objection arises because the people of any society who are immersed in eating and drinking have no connection with God, so they cannot understand how a human being could have a connection with God.

The fact is that material prosperity corrupts human nature; it makes the mind dull, closes the doors of the heart, and the hearts of the pleasure-seekers turn to stone. Within them no sensitivity remains, so they are neither affected by any matter nor do they accept anything. For this reason prosperous people always oppose the Islamic movement, and therefore Islam opposes luxury and fashions its collective system in such a way that there is no room in it for the mutrafeen (the affluent who indulge in luxury), because these people become the stench of society; they pollute the whole environment and make society so filthy that worms breed within it, and such a society is at last consumed by those worms.

Moreover, they did not believe in resurrection after death. They used to say: how will human beings be raised after death and after they have turned to dust? This is far from possible, and what this messenger tells us is strange.

Ya'iduhu annakum idhaa mittum wa kuntum turaaban wa 'izaaman annakum mukhrajoon (23:35), haihaata haihaata limaa tu'adoon (23:36), in hiya illaa hayaatunaa ad-dunyaa namootu wa nahyaa wa maa nahnu bi-mab'ootheen (23:37): "Does he tell you that when you have died and become dust and bones, you will be brought out (from the graves)? Far, far is what you are promised! There is only our life of this world: we die and we live, and we shall never be raised. This man is only fabricating a lie about Allah, and we will never believe him." The truth is that people with such thinking cannot grasp the reality of the life to come. They have neither reflected upon the profound realities of life nor tried to understand its intricate system, nor do such people understand the priorities of a higher and more exalted life. These lofty purposes of life cannot be fulfilled in this world. In this world the good is not fully rewarded, nor is evil fully requited. This complete reward and punishment will be given in the Hereafter. In the Hereafter the people of faith will attain the highest and most excellent standard of life, where there is neither fear nor weariness. Likewise, those who adopt disbelief and wickedness will reach a most humiliating and degraded state in which their humanity is destroyed, and there they will continue to burn like firewood, being burned. Their punishment will not be lessened, nor will the reward of the people of faith be diminished.

Such mutrafeen cannot comprehend these lofty purposes and such profound meanings. It is astonishing that these people do not reflect upon the various stages and phases of their own present life, which have just been set before them in this very surah. They cannot draw the conclusion from this wondrous self-operating system of creation that, by a similar self-operating system, Allah will restore to life the dust and the skeletal frame. Therefore they are astonished by this messenger's report that they will be brought out from their graves. Now, with great arrogance and pride, they display their wisdom: this is life and this is death; one generation dies and another remains alive. For those who have died and become dust and bones, it is far from possible that they should return. This report that this messenger is giving, and his promise to us that we shall be raised again, is beyond possibility.

These people do not stop at their ignorance of failing to understand that one will be raised after death; rather, they go further and accuse their messenger of fabricating lies about Allah on his own account, although they do not know Allah at all. They mention the name of Allah only at this moment, and they mention it only so that they may level accusations against the messenger.

In innahoo illaa rajulun bihi jinnatun fa-tarabbasoo bihi hattaa heen (23:25) ... [verse 38 as quoted:] In huwa illaa rajulun iftaraa 'alallahi kadhiban wa ma nahnu lahu bi-mu'mineen (23:38): "This man is only fabricating a lie against Allah, and we will never believe him." In such circumstances, what else can this messenger (ﷺ) do but seek help from his Lord, just as Hadrat Nuh (alayhis salam) sought help from his Lord before him. The prayer of Hadrat Nuh for help was also this:

Qaala rabbi-nsurni bima kaddhaboon (23:39): The messenger said: "O my Lord, help me, because they have denied me." Allah's answer comes: the respite of this people ends, because no goodness remains in them; these people are immersed in heedlessness, denial and obstinacy.

Qaala 'ammaa qaleelin la-yusbihunna nadimeen (23:40): It was said in reply: "Soon they will surely become regretful for what they have done." But at that time their regret will not benefit them.

Fa-akhadhathumu-s-sayhatu bil-haqqi fa-ja'alnaahum ghuthaa'an (23:41): "Then a great cry seized them, in accordance with the truth, and We made them mere refuse (ghuthaa')." Ghuthaa' refers to the rubbish that a flood carries away and casts aside, in which nothing is of any use. Such refuse is of no value and is a heap of every kind of filth and useless things. Since these people had given up those human qualities by which they were honoured as human beings, and since they could not grasp the wisdom of their worldly and otherworldly existence, and had severed all their ties with their Creator, no quality remained within them through which they could be honoured or continue to exist in this world. Therefore they were swept away like the rubbish carried by a flood, cast aside in such a way that none remained to ask after them. This is the unique style of the Qur'an, which expresses a reality with extraordinary force and brevity.

For the further disgrace of these people, and to show the manner of their expulsion by Allah, this phrase is sufficient: that they were removed far from the mercy of Allah.

Fa-bu'dan li-l-qawmi-z-zalimeen (23:41): "Away with the wrongdoing people!" Far from life, far from good remembrance, far from the realm of reality, and far also from the realm of conscience.

After this, the discourse advances the theme: peoples come upon the stage and depart.

Far, far is what you are promised! There is only our life of this world: we die and we live, and we shall never be raised. This man is only fabricating a lie about Allah, and we will never believe him." The truth is that people with such thinking cannot grasp the reality of the life to come. They have neither reflected upon the profound realities of life nor tried to understand its intricate system, nor do such people understand the priorities of a higher and more exalted life. These lofty purposes of life cannot be fulfilled in this world. In this world the good is not fully rewarded, nor is evil fully requited. This complete reward and punishment will be given in the Hereafter. In the Hereafter the people of faith will attain the highest and most excellent standard of life, where there is neither fear nor weariness. Likewise, those who adopt disbelief and wickedness will reach a most humiliating and degraded state in which their humanity is destroyed, and there they will continue to burn like firewood, being burned. Their punishment will not be lessened, nor will the reward of the people of faith be diminished.

Such mutrafeen cannot comprehend these lofty purposes and such profound meanings. It is astonishing that these people do not reflect upon the various stages and phases of their own present life, which have just been set before them in this very surah. They cannot draw the conclusion from this wondrous self-operating system of creation that, by a similar self-operating system, Allah will restore to life the dust and the skeletal frame. Therefore they are astonished by this messenger's report that they will be brought out from their graves. Now, with great arrogance and pride, they display their wisdom: this is life and this is death; one generation dies and another remains alive. For those who have died and become dust and bones, it is far from possible that they should return. This report that this messenger is giving, and his promise to us that we shall be raised again, is beyond possibility.

These people do not stop at their ignorance of failing to understand that one will be raised after death; rather, they go further and accuse their messenger of fabricating lies about Allah on his own account, although they do not know Allah at all. They mention the name of Allah only at this moment, and they mention it only so that they may level accusations against the messenger.

In innahoo illaa rajulun bihi jinnatun fa-tarabbasoo bihi hattaa heen (23:25) ... [verse 38 as quoted:] In huwa illaa rajulun iftaraa 'alallahi kadhiban wa ma nahnu lahu bi-mu'mineen (23:38): "This man is only fabricating a lie against Allah, and we will never believe him." In such circumstances, what else can this messenger (ﷺ) do but seek help from his Lord, just as Hadrat Nuh (alayhis salam) sought help from his Lord before him. The prayer of Hadrat Nuh for help was also this:

Qaala rabbi-nsurni bima kaddhaboon (23:39): The messenger said: "O my Lord, help me, because they have denied me." Allah's answer comes: the respite of this people ends, because no goodness remains in them; these people are immersed in heedlessness, denial and obstinacy.

Qaala 'ammaa qaleelin la-yusbihunna nadimeen (23:40): It was said in reply: "Soon they will surely become regretful for what they have done." But at that time their regret will not benefit them.

Fa-akhadhathumu-s-sayhatu bil-haqqi fa-ja'alnaahum ghuthaa'an (23:41): "Then a great cry seized them, in accordance with the truth, and We made them mere refuse (ghuthaa')." Ghuthaa' refers to the rubbish that a flood carries away and casts aside, in which nothing is of any use. Such refuse is of no value and is a heap of every kind of filth and useless things. Since these people had given up those human qualities by which they were honoured as human beings, and since they could not grasp the wisdom of their worldly and otherworldly existence, and had severed all their ties with their Creator, no quality remained within them through which they could be honoured or continue to exist in this world. Therefore they were swept away like the rubbish carried by a flood, cast aside in such a way that none remained to ask after them. This is the unique style of the Qur'an, which expresses a reality with extraordinary force and brevity.

For the further disgrace of these people, and to show the manner of their expulsion by Allah, this phrase is sufficient: that they were removed far from the mercy of Allah.

Fa-bu'dan li-l-qawmi-z-zalimeen (23:41): "Away with the wrongdoing people!" Far from life, far from good remembrance, far from the realm of reality, and far also from the realm of conscience.

After this, the discourse advances the theme: peoples come upon the stage and depart.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 23, verses 42–44:

Then We raised after them other generations. (Verses 42–44)

Here a summary of the whole history of Islamic invitation (da'wah) is presented, and within this summary is also stated the Sunnah of Allah which operates throughout this universe. This history begins with the people of Noah and the people of Hud, 'Ad, and concludes with Musa and Isa (peace be upon them). This was the summary of the intervening centuries, and the divine Sunnah is this:

﴿Not before its time does any nation precede its term, nor do they delay.﴾ (23:43)

﴿Every time a messenger came to a nation, they denied him.﴾ (23:44)

And whenever nations denied the messengers, Allah seized those nations. This Sunnah of Allah has continued throughout the whole of human history.

﴿So We followed some of them with others.﴾ (23:44)

﴿We made them into tales.﴾ (23:44)

That is: We destroyed nations one after another, and after their destruction only a lesson remained and nothing else. People retained only the cautionary tales of them. This summary also ends with a humiliating exile and a curse: ﴿Away with them, the wicked ones.﴾ (23:44)

﴿So away with the people who do not believe.﴾ (23:44)

After this, a summary of the story of Musa (peace be upon him) is given, and this account likewise proceeds towards the same goal and in the same manner.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 23, verses 45–48:

Then We sent Our messengers, one after another (thumma arsalna)... [heading: "Then We sent from among those destroyed" – ثم ارسلنا من المھلکین (verses 45 to 48)]

In this summary too, their objection stands out clearly: why are these messengers human beings like us, and mere mortals?

﴿Fa qalu a-nu'minu labasharayni mithlina wa qawmuhuma lana 'abidun﴾ (23:47) – "Shall we believe in two men like ourselves, when their people are our servants?" That is: first, for the people, it was an insult to Musa and Harun (peace be upon them) that they belonged to that (enslaved) people.

It is surprising that the clear signs and great miracles presented by Musa and Harun had no effect on these people. This was because seals had been placed upon their hearts; these people were immersed in the conditions and grandeur of this earth, although this whole world and its grandeur is a worthless thing, and in comparison to faith it is not worth a blade of grass.

Now there comes a brief allusion to Isa son of Maryam (peace be upon him) as well. He himself was a miracle. He too was denied in the same way.

The commentary on the verses 49–50 of Surah al-Mu'minun (23) reads:

"And We made the son of Maryam and his mother a sign, and We sheltered them on a high ground, a place of settled calm and flowing water." (Qur'an 23:50, as rendered here in translation.)

Regarding the Rabwah mentioned in these verses, the reports differ as to where it is. Was it in Egypt, in Damascus, or in Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem)? These are the places to which Maryam took her child, Isa, in his childhood. There are detailed accounts of this in the books of the Christians. Here, it is of no importance where this Rabwah was. The purpose was that Allah kept Maryam and the son of Maryam in the most pure place for the whole period. This place was green, water was abundant, and they lived there in great joy and comfort.

Having reached this point, Allah addresses this community and congregation of all the Messengers as though that entire congregation, in terms of one field, one mission and one call, are links of one and the same chain.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 23, verses 51–52:

﴿Yā ayyuhā al-rusul fa-ttaqūn﴾ (Verses 51 to 52)

Here, in the address to the Messengers, their humanity is highlighted, because the objection of the peoples of the Messengers was that the Messengers were human beings. Why are they human?

﴿Kulū min al-ṭayyibāt﴾ (23:51): "Eat of the good things." Eating is a distinctive feature of humanity. But by attaching the qualifier "good" (ṭayyibāt), it is shown that the humanity of the Messengers is exalted. They elevate all of humanity, purify all people, and connect them to the higher world.

Then, in this same address, it is said: do good deeds. That is, reform this earth. Therefore, action too is a requirement of humanity. But people do both good and bad deeds, whereas the Messengers motivate people toward good deeds. The Messengers set the rule for people's conduct, define the purposes of their actions, and through their own actions they are linked to the higher world.

It is not the work of the Messengers to free themselves from humanity; rather, their purpose is to raise humanity up. For this they set lofty horizons and lofty aims. It is God's desire that in the world human beings be righteous, pure and distinguished, with the Messengers as their leaders, carrying people to heights. And in the Hereafter, it is God alone who will determine their worth by His extremely precise measure.

﴿Innī bimā ta'malūna ʿalīm﴾ (23:51): "Indeed, I am All-Knowing of what you do." Here, the distances of time are erased and the distances of space come to an end, because the message is one, which these Messengers brought.

Their disposition is one; they are distinguished from other people; and the direction of all the Messengers is one and the same.

﴿Wa-inna hādhihi ummatukum ummatan wāḥidatan wa-anā rabbukum fa-ttaqūn﴾ (23:52): "And indeed this, your community, is a single community, and I am your Lord, so fear Me alone."

**Lesson 50 at a Glance**

This is the third lesson of this Surah. After describing the circumstances of the Messengers, it now portrays the state of the people at the time when the final Messenger came. Among the people there were severe religious differences, and even on the doctrine of Tawhid, which all the Messengers had unanimously taught, there were disagreements.

The people also treated the truth that the Seal of the Prophets (ﷺ) brought with heedlessness, although they should have reflected on this new call and on those who accepted it. The character of the believers stood before them. They worshipped Allah, did righteous deeds, and feared the Hereafter. The thought that one day they would stand before their Lord made their hearts tremble. These are two tenants of two kinds. There is complete contrast between these two groups: the believers are awake and fearful, while the disbelievers are heedless and senseless.

In this lesson of the Surah, the position of the disbelievers is criticized and their doubts are answered. Their conscience is awakened so that they reflect on the proofs of faith present within themselves and in the horizons. Then their own accepted beliefs are taken up, and the argument against them is established from those very beliefs. Finally, it is said: leave them to their own state until they reach their appointed end. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is told to continue on his path and not to be distressed or disheartened by their obstinacy and stubbornness. Rather, he should respond to their evil conduct with good conduct, and seek Allah's refuge from the accursed Satan, who is misguiding these people.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 23, verses 55–56:

Verses 53 to 56: "Then they divided their affair among themselves into sects, each party rejoicing in what it has."

In the account of the messengers it was said that they were one community. Their word was one, their call was one, their worship was for the One God alone, and their ideological direction was one. But after the messengers, people split into groups and sects, and they did not remain agreed upon any one path (minhaj).

The Qur'an portrays this division in an remarkably vivid, sensory manner. They tore their religion apart among themselves into pieces. Each seized a piece. Whatever portion came into the hand of each sect or group, it ran off with it, content that the true piece was in its own hand, and so it did not look back. Each group sat down with its piece and stopped thinking about any other matter, lest any word or argument reach its mind and bring light. They became content with what they had, and deprived themselves of every kind of light and guidance. What an excellent depiction this is of sectarianism and factionalism.

Having drawn this picture, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is addressed thus:

"So leave them in their heedlessness for a while" (23:54). That is, leave them in the circumstances in which they are immersed, let them remain drowned in their state, and let the end that awaits them overtake them suddenly, because after respite that end is certain.

Here the Qur'an, mocking their heedlessness and stagnation, says: what do they think of the respite being given to them and the wealth, property and children with which they are being favored? Do they imagine that Allah is pleased with them and bestowing upon them, that they are beloved servants upon whom the rain of gifts is falling?

"Do they think that We extend to them wealth and children, hastening to them in good things?" (23:55–56a). "Do they reckon that We are supplying them with wealth and children, as though We were hastening to them with good things? Nay, but they do not perceive" (23:56). That is, they cannot even conceive what calamity will come upon them after this wealth and offspring, nor how general and all-encompassing that calamity will be.

On one side are these people, immersed in heedlessness and astray; on the other side are those who are always awake and very cautious in the matter of their Lord.

The commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 23, verses 57–61:

Al-ladhina yusari'un (verses 57 to 61)

This shows what effects faith has upon the human heart. Its sensitivity becomes acute; intense fear and extreme caution are born within it, and in this world a person thinks of perfection and lofty heights. He cares for the Hereafter, even though he carries out in this world the duties and obligations imposed upon him by God; that is, he does not adopt worldliness here.

Just consider: these believers tremble with the fear of God. They live their lives with the utmost caution.

They have faith in the signs of God. They associate no one with God. They continue to discharge the duties and obligations imposed by God. In all other acts of worship they are engaged to the extent of their capacity. Yet despite all these deeds, "those who give what they give, and their hearts tremble" (23:60), "that they will surely return to their Lord". They feel that some shortcoming must have occurred on their part in regard to God, although they have served Him to the best of their ability; yet in their own eyes their deeds seem meagre.

It is narrated from Hadrat Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her) that she said: "O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), does the verse 'those who give what they give, while their hearts tremble' (23:60) refer to a person who steals, commits adultery and drinks wine, but then fears Allah?" He (ﷺ) said: "No, O daughter of Siddiq; rather it refers to the person who prays, fasts, gives his wealth in charity, and still fears Allah." (Tirmidhi)

The heart of a believer is conscious that the hand of Allah is upon him. He feels that in every breath the mercies of Allah rain upon him like rain. Just reflect upon the movement of the heart alone, what a great mercy it is. Therefore the believer regards his worship and obedience as little, for in comparison with the mercy and grace of Allah, his service is nothing. He finds the majesty and greatness of Allah in every particle of his being. In his consciousness it is firmly settled that everything is in the hand of Allah, and therefore he remains fearful at all times, trembling. He is afraid that suddenly he will be presented before Allah, and his bundle of shortcomings will be laid open before Him, and the result will be that he did not render the due of worship or give thanks for Allah's bounties and favours; then what will his condition be, and what answer will he give?

Such people are indeed the ones who hasten forward in good works; and such people are foremost in goodness, and it is such people who perform every noble task of Islam: alert of mind, active, and forward-moving obedient servants. In comparison with them, those who are immersed in ease and pleasure are of no use; those who are in deep heedlessness, who think that they are privileged by God with special favours and that good is all theirs. They are heedless in the way that prey grazes in its heedlessness while in truth it is moving towards its snare. It thinks it has found food, and suddenly it is caught in the trap. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 23, verse 62:

﴿وَلَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا وَلَدَيْنَا كِتَابٌ يَنطِقُ بِالْحَقِّ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ﴾ (آیت نمبر 26)

Translation: "And We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity. And with Us is a Record which speaks with truth, and they will not be wronged."

Allah has imposed certain obligations upon mankind, but He has imposed these obligations and duties in accordance with human capacity. Allah knows well that man is His creation, and He will reckon only those deeds which lie within the limits of their capacity. Allah does not do injustice to human beings by loading upon them a burden they cannot bear. Nor will Allah leave out or cancel anything of their deeds. Whatever they do, its account will be recorded.

﴿يَنطِقُ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ (23:62) "It will tell the truth precisely." It will lay everything open. Allah is the best of reckoners. Then why do people neglect? "It will tell the truth precisely." It will lay everything open. Allah is the best of reckoners. Then why do people neglect?

Because their hearts are unaware of the reality. That light has not entered them which gives life to hearts. Because these people, leaving that light, have become occupied with other affairs and have gone far ahead in those preoccupations. When they come to their senses, there will be a painful punishment before them, and along with that punishment there will be reproach and rebuke, and they will have to face a humiliating treatment.

**Bal qulubuhum tahjurun (Verses 62–67)**

These people are not immersed in the circumstances they are engaged in because the Messengers impose on them commands beyond their capacity. The real cause is that they are sunk in heedlessness and pay no attention to the truth that the Qur'an presents. Instead, they drift along other paths, and these paths are contrary to Islam.

﴿And they have deeds other than that, which they are doing.﴾ (23:63)

The scene now presented is of the moment when God's punishment seizes them. This punishment is devastating, sudden, and overtakes them all at once.

﴿Until, when We seize their affluent ones with punishment, behold, they begin to cry out.﴾ (23:64)

It is the habit of the wealthy that they often become deeply immersed in luxury, intoxication and revelry, and they pay no heed to the consequences of these indulgences. Now observe their condition: when God's punishment suddenly overtakes them, they begin to shriek and wail. Now they call out in supplication and seek mercy. This state arises because they were immersed in luxury, were heedless, and were arrogant and proud. Yet instead of softening towards this outcry and supplication and showing mercy, they are received with rebuke, reproach and harsh scolding.

﴿Do not cry out today; you will not be helped by Us.﴾ (23:65)

This scene is before us: these criminals are being scolded, and they are given a despairing reply, denying them any kind of help or leniency. Along with this, they are being reminded of how they were sunk in heedlessness and what their reaction was to the Islamic call.

﴿My verses were recited to you, but you used to turn back on your heels.﴾ (23:66)

That is, they used to turn away and flee backwards on their heels, as though what was being recited to them was some dangerous matter or some extremely loathsome affair from which one must keep away. They considered themselves gravely wronged by believing in the truth. Not only did they turn and flee, but in the nightly gatherings they held in their courtyards, they used extremely disparaging language about the Islamic call, and it was a subject of mockery for them.

These people used the most vulgar language about Islam in their gatherings. They used to hold these gatherings sitting around their idols in the Ka'bah. The Qur'an paints a very vivid picture of their pastimes, while now, after the punishment has come, they cry out intensely and seek help. The Qur'an reminds them to recall those gatherings. This portrayal is made in such a manner as if the event is happening right now, as if they are seeing that night and living in those very circumstances. Such a portrayal of the scenes of the Day of Judgment is a distinctive style of the Qur'an. (See my book *Al-Tasvir al-Fanni fi al-Quran* [The Artistic Portrayal in the Qur'an].)

The polytheists used to raise objections against the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the Qur'an in their assemblies, and in keeping with the morals of the Days of Ignorance (*Jahiliyyah*) they took pride in this attitude. They were not in a position to understand the truth of the Qur'an, because they were blind to insight. Far from accepting the truth, they used to mock the Qur'an and level accusations against the Prophet (ﷺ). This has been the same case in every age. In every *Jahiliyyah* this is what happens. Let it be remembered that the *Jahiliyyah* of the Arabs was also one of the many *Jahiliyyahs*, and that several *Jahiliyyahs* came and went until the revelation of the Qur'an, and will continue to come after it as well.

From this scene of the Day of Judgment, the Qur'an transfers these people back to the world. Now they are in the world again. In this scene, they themselves are asked why they adopted such strange and unreasonable a position, and what sound reason there is that these people do not believe in the trustworthy Messenger (ﷺ). What doubts are these that create confusion in their hearts and keep them from the path of guidance? What arguments are these on which they base their denial and their nonsense in their assemblies, when the religion of Islam is a straightforward, simple, true religion, the Straight Path?

What arguments are these on which they base their denial and their nonsense in their assemblies, when the religion of Islam is a straightforward, simple, true religion, the Straight Path?

These people are not immersed in the circumstances they are engaged in because the Messengers impose on them commands beyond their capacity. The real cause is that they are sunk in heedlessness and pay no attention to the truth that the Qur'an presents. Instead, they drift along other paths, and these paths are contrary to Islam.

﴿And they have deeds other than that, which they are doing.﴾ (23:63)

The scene now presented is of the moment when God's punishment seizes them. This punishment is devastating, sudden, and overtakes them all at once.

﴿Until, when We seize their affluent ones with punishment, behold, they begin to cry out.﴾ (23:64)

It is the habit of the wealthy that they often become deeply immersed in luxury, intoxication and revelry, and they pay no heed to the consequences of these indulgences. Now observe their condition: when God's punishment suddenly overtakes them, they begin to shriek and wail. Now they call out in supplication and seek mercy. This state arises because they were immersed in luxury, were heedless, and were arrogant and proud. Yet instead of softening towards this outcry and supplication and showing mercy, they are received with rebuke, reproach and harsh scolding.

﴿Do not cry out today; you will not be helped by Us.﴾ (23:65)

This scene is before us: these criminals are being scolded, and they are given a despairing reply, denying them any kind of help or leniency. Along with this, they are being reminded of how they were sunk in heedlessness and what their reaction was to the Islamic call.

﴿My verses were recited to you, but you used to turn back on your heels.﴾ (23:66)

That is, they used to turn away and flee backwards on their heels, as though what was being recited to them was some dangerous matter or some extremely loathsome affair from which one must keep away. **Commentary of Sayyid Qutb, *Fi Zilal al-Quran*, on Surah al-Mu'minun (23), verses 68–70**

**﴿Afalam yadabbaru l-qawl﴾ (Verses 68–74)**

If anyone reflects even slightly on the teachings presented by the Prophet (ﷺ), it is impossible that he would turn away from them, because this speech possesses great beauty, great perfection, and great attractiveness. Its teachings are thoroughly natural and in accordance with human reason and intuition. They contain nourishment for the heart and the mind, and their orientation is highly constructive. The system and law they present are extremely firm. When one observes all these teachings, human nature accepts them. Yet the reality is that the deniers have not reflected (tadabbur) upon this speech at all. This is why they turn away from it.

﴿Afalam yadabbaru l-qawl﴾ (23:68): "Have they not then pondered over the Word?"

﴿Am ja'a hum ma lam ya'ti aba'ahumu l-awwalin﴾ (23:68): "Or has there come to them something that did not come to their forefathers of old?" That is, is the sending of a Messenger something unfamiliar to them and their ancestors? Their traditions contain no precedent of a messenger coming to them, or of someone presenting to them ideas and beliefs like the call to the Oneness of God. Yet the history of the Messengers shows that Messengers came one after another, and all of them taught what the final Prophet (ﷺ) is teaching now. Moreover, the Prophet (ﷺ) has knowledge about several of these earlier Messengers.

﴿Am lam ya'rifu rasulahum fahum lahu munkirun﴾ (23:69): "Or did they not recognise their Messenger, so that they deny him?" That is, the cause of their illness cannot be that they do not know the Messenger who has come. They know this Messenger very well. They know his personality, they know his lineage, and they are well informed about his self and his qualities. They know with certainty that he is truthful and trustworthy, and before his prophethood they themselves had given him the titles "the Truthful" and "the Trustworthy."

﴿Am yaqulna bihi jinnah﴾ (23:70): "Or do they say, 'He has a madness'?" Some of the foolish among them did level this accusation against him. But it was merely an accusation. In their hearts they too knew that he was wise and perfect, since throughout his life they had never heard of any lapse on his part.

There was no room for any of the above doubts. Then why do they not accept the truth? The real reason is that most of them disliked the truth, because the truth that he brought was snatching away from them the false values in which they lived and which they regarded as sacred. This truth opposed their carnal desires and the habits deeply rooted and entrenched in their lives.

﴿Bal ja'a hum bil-haqqi wa akthariham lil-haqqi karihun﴾ (23:70): "Rather, he has brought them the truth, but most of them are averse to the truth." Truth is truth; it cannot change to suit their desires. The stability of the heavens and the earth rests upon truth. The law that operates over this universe is in fact the truth. It is in accordance with this law and this truth that the universe and all existing things within it are running.

﴿Wa lawi ttaba'a l-haqqu ahwa'ahum lafasadati s-samawatu wal-ardu wa man fihinna﴾ (23:71): "And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and all who are in them would have been corrupted." Truth is one and fixed, whereas the desires of each person are separate and constantly changing. This entire universe follows the truth, and its path is one. Its principle and its law do not change, nor does any transient desire bring about any alteration in this law. If the system of the universe were to become subject to people's wishes and changing desires, and to follow their fleeting urges, then this entire order of the world would fall into corruption. The conditions and ways of people would be ruined, and the foundations of life and of good and evil would be altered. If one person is pleased, his values would be one way, and if another is displeased, his standards and measures would be different. Likewise, people's standards change with their varying likes and dislikes, their inclinations and fears, and their joys and sorrows, because human temperament does not remain in one state; afflictions keep coming upon it. Truth, however, remains in its place. The system of the universe, and its purposes, demand that its order remain stable, coherent and continuous, that the universe operate according to firm and unchanging laws, and that its system be free from fluctuation and uncertainty.

Since the system of the universe is founded upon truth and is being run in accordance with truth, Allah has likewise established for human life a code based on truth. This code has also been set by the One who runs the whole universe. Just as the law of the universe is immutable, so this human code is immutable as well, because man too is a part of the universe, so that human conduct and the course of the universe may be in harmony. Therefore, truth requires that the Creator of this universe be also the Author and Lawgiver of the human code of life, so that the movement of man is in harmony with the movement of the universe. If the regulation of human life were left to their desires, the order of human life would fall into corruption and disorder would set in.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 23, verse 71:

"And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been corrupted" (23:71). Therefore this system is wholly subject to the truth; it obeys the truth and runs in accordance with the status of the Governor of the universe.

This truth has come to the Ummah, and it is more deserving that it submit to it. Firstly, this is a matter of truth; secondly, it is a great honour for this Ummah. Moreover, this truthfulness is also the identity of this Ummah. The reality is that, had there been no Islam, what other identity would the Arabs have had among the nations of the world, and had there been no Islam, where would the Muslims have been?

Before Islam, the Arabs had no mention in the history of nations, nor did they have any role. Then, as long as the Arabs held fast to the Qur'an, their voice resounded throughout the universe; and when the Arabs abandoned the Qur'an, their role in history diminished and faded away, until they became unworthy of mention, and they will never again attain any station unless they adopt their true title and their true identity. Since these people were given the call to the truth, and they rejected it and instead began to accuse the one who called to the truth, and adopted a false position, therefore, in keeping with the theme of this passage, the address now turns to their false position. Their wrong attitude is condemned, and the accusations they made against the Trustworthy Messenger (ﷺ) are refuted.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 23, verse 72:

Am tas'aluhum kharja (23:72): "Or are you asking them for some payment?" Are you demanding a heavy fee for this guidance and instruction, which they are unable to pay and from which they are fleeing? You do not ask anything of them at all, for your reward is with Allah.

Fakharaju Rabbika khayrun wa huwa khayr ar-raziqeen (23:72): "The provision of your Lord is better, and He is the best of providers." No prophet ever seeks any compensation from people, whereas human beings are very weak, poor and needy. The prophet is connected and bound to Allah, in whose treasures there is no shortage. Rather, even the helpers of the prophet do not seek any of the worldly benefits of this world, because their eyes are also fixed on the reward that is prepared for them with Allah, and in this world they are content with it, whether it is little or much. The truth is that when a person's soul is joined with Allah, then this work no longer remains equal to the entire universe and its contents for him. Indeed, the reality is that you are guiding these people toward a system that is extremely firm.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 23, verse 73:

﴿And indeed, you call them to a straight path.﴾ You are calling them to the law of nature (nāmūs-i-fitrat), bringing them into harmony with that caravan, and leading them straight toward the Creator of the universe.

The condition of these people is just like the condition of all those who do not believe and stray from the right path.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 23, verse 74:

Verse 73: "Those who do not believe in the Hereafter are indeed deviating from the path" [wa inna alladhina la yu'minuna bil-akhirati ʿani al-sirati lanakibun] — "But those who do not believe in the Hereafter want to walk away from the right path."

If they were guided, they would reflect with their hearts and minds upon this life, and as a result of that reflection a human being inevitably comes to believe in the Hereafter. He necessarily becomes convinced of a world in which this life will exist in its most complete state, and in which people will receive full justice, because the Hereafter is the final link in the order of the universe, in which the planning of Allah for the universe will reach its conclusion.

These people who do not believe in the Hereafter and have strayed from the right path: even if they are given great wealth and are tested, they still do not come to the right path; and even if they are tested by being struck with hardships, they still do not come to the right path. When they are blessed with favours, they say:

"Innama numidduhum bihi min mal wa banin. Nusari'u lahum fi al-khayrat" (23:55–56) — "What We have given them in wealth and children is so that We may hasten to them with good things."

And when a punishment comes upon them, their hearts do not soften, their consciences do not awaken, and they do not humble themselves before Allah to remove this calamity so that He may relieve them of it. They will remain in this state until the Day of Resurrection, when the punishment of Allah will seize them, and there they will be left in despair and bewilderment.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 23, verses 75–77:

﴿وَلَوْ رَحِمْنَاهُم وَكَشَفْنَا مَا بِهِم مِّن ضُرٍّ لَّلَجُّوا فِي طُغْيَانِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ﴾ ” ۔ ۔ “

This is the attitude of some people in the future. They are hard-hearted. They are heedless of Allah and deny the Hereafter. The polytheists of Makkah were among the people of this kind whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had to deal with.

If a person is struck by a calamity and begins to humble himself and supplicate before Allah, this is a sign of turning back to Allah (rujoo' ila Allah). It is a sign that there is an awareness of God in the heart of such a person, and the notion that the final refuge is Allah. A heart that turns to Allah in this way is soft, awake, and benefits from admonition. This awareness protects a person from heedlessness and slipping. Such people derive benefit and admonition from afflictions and difficulties. But when someone goes far ahead in his misguidance and rebellion and becomes blind, one should despair of that person. There remains no hope of his reform. He should be left to fall prey to the punishment of the Hereafter, and that Hereafter will come very suddenly. It will suddenly confront everyone, and all people will then be bewildered and distressed, and will despair that any escape is now possible.

Once again an attempt is made to awaken their consciousness and intuition. The summary of the proofs of faith in the self and in the horizons is presented. Reference is made to matters that are apparent and yet have been neglected.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 23, verses 75–77:

Once again an attempt is made to awaken their consciousness and intuition. The summary of the proofs of faith in the self and in the horizons is presented. Reference is made to matters that are apparent and yet have been neglected.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 23, verse 78:

﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي﴾ ... ﴿تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ (78 to 80)

If a person reflects upon his own creation and his own form and appearance, and reflects upon his various organs and limbs, his senses and his perceptions, then recognizing the Creator is not a difficult matter. By contemplating these wondrous things, he can attain knowledge (ma'rifah) of the Creator of the universe, for who other than Allah has displayed these miracles? In this universe there are countless wonders, small and great.

Let a person reflect just on his faculty of hearing. How does this faculty work? How does it receive sounds and derive meanings from sounds? Let him reflect on the faculty of sight. How does a person see? How does the eye take in light and perceive images? Then there is the mind and its perception, which determines the value of things and of gratitude, and determines concepts and standards. In short, if one reflects upon all the faculties, perceptions and sensations, each one is a marvel.

If one reflects only upon the five senses and the manner in which they function, this alone is a great miracle within the world of humanity. As for the creation of these faculties, the structure of their present form and shape, and their harmony with the whole universe, so that if even one of the relationships that exist between the forces of the universe and human faculties were to disappear, the entire system would be disrupted, the ear would be unable to hear, the eye unable to see; yet the governing power of Allah the Exalted has made them thus. But man is so ungrateful that he does not reflect upon these blessings of Allah.

﴿قَلِيلًا مَا تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ (23:78): "Little is it that you give thanks." Gratitude can only occur when a person knows the One who bestowed a blessing, knows His being and attributes, worships and serves Allah alone, and also knows that these faculties have been given to man by that Being, through which he enjoys comfort and luxury on this earth and benefits from everything.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 23, verse 79:

﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي ذَرَأَكُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ "It is He who multiplied you upon the earth, and made you His vicegerents (khalifah) and holders of authority over it on His behalf. Then He gave you the faculties of sight and hearing, the faculty of thought, and all the other capacities that were necessary for the discharge of the duty of earthly vicegerency (khilafat-i-arziyyah)."

﴿وَإِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ﴾ "And to Him you will be gathered." Then there He will call you to account for whether you discharged the duty of vicegerency on earth in accordance with Allah's guidance or not, whether you did good or evil, whether you remained upon guidance or adopted the path of misguidance. For you were not created in vain, nor were you left on this earth like unbridled camels without a rope. Rather, your creation took place under wisdom and planning.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 23, verse 80:**

﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ﴾ (23:80) "It is He who gives life and causes death." Death and life are events that appear in succession, like night and day. The mastery of life and death belongs to Allah alone. Man, who is a more developed animal, has no power to create life, and man cannot even take life from any living creature. For you have not been created in vain, nor have you been left in this earth as unrestrained creatures. Rather, your creation occurred under wisdom and planning.

﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ﴾ (23:80) "It is He who gives life and causes death." Death and life are events that appear in succession, like night and day. The mastery of life and death belongs to Allah alone. Man, who is a more developed ... [the following sentence is garbled in the source: "انسان جو زیادہ ترقی یافتہ ہیں جو رات اور دن نمودار ہوتے ہیں ۔ موت وحیات کا مالک صرف اللہ ہے۔ انسان جو زیادہ ترقی یافتہ حیوان ہے"] is a more developed animal; he has no power to create even a single cell of life, and man cannot take life from any living creature. For the One who grants life is the One who knows its reality. It is within the power of that Being to grant life and to take it back. Man sometimes becomes the cause of someone's life being taken, but in reality man cannot take anyone's life from them. In truth, life and death are in the hand of Allah alone. Besides Him, no one has the authority to decide life and death.

﴿وَلَهُ اخْتِلَافُ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ ۚ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ (23:80) "And His is the alternation of night and day. Will you not then use reason?" The alternation of night and day is in the control of Allah. He alone owns it and alone has authority over it, just as He alone owns life and death. The alternation of night and day is also a cosmic Sunnah of Allah (Sunnah Ilahiyyah, the divine way or law), and just as the functioning of life and death follows the Sunnah of Allah, so too do the human soul, the human body, this universe, and these heavens all run according to that Sunnah. If Allah removes life from someone's body, the body becomes cold. Similarly, if Allah withdrew light from the earth, it would remain in darkness. Here Allah has created life and created light, and by these two the course of life moves on. And it will keep moving for as long as Allah wills.

﴿أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ (23:80) "Will you not then use reason?" That is, so that you may comprehend the reality of these things. All these things are evidence of the existence of the Creator and of His craftsmanship: that He is the Creator and Manager, and that He runs this entire universe.

Now that the discussion with them is concluded, a positive comment is made on it: the statements these people make about resurrection after death and accountability have been made by earlier peoples as well.

Rather, they said the like of what the former people said (Verses 81–82)

At first glance this is an extremely reprehensible matter, because despite these clear verses and these proofs and the proofs of the universe, the things people say are reprehensible. Human faculties themselves, the human power of hearing, power of sight and power of reflection, have been given to him so that he is a responsible and accountable being. He is answerable for his deeds and thoughts. If he does good deeds, he will deserve their reward, and if he does evil deeds, he will deserve punishment. In this world it is clearly seen that sometimes a person receives the reward he deserves, and sometimes he does not receive the punishment he deserves; therefore the establishment of the Hereafter is also rationally necessary.

Allah causes death at every moment and also keeps giving life. For Allah there is no difficult problem in how He will raise them again, since Allah is constantly giving life to various things, and the flood of life flows on this earth.

As for the disbelievers, not only have their faculties of perception failed to grasp resurrection after death and failed to understand the wisdom of Allah contained in it, but they also mock this belief. They say: "Our forefathers too were threatened with the Resurrection, but so far this Resurrection has not come."

The Qur'an quotes the disbelievers: ﴿We have been promised this, we and our fathers before us. This is nothing but the fables of the ancients.﴾ "Yes, we have heard many promises, and our forefathers too have been hearing them. These are merely the tales of bygone times."

But for resurrection after death (ba'th ba'd al-mawt), a time has been fixed. Allah has fixed it by His own planning and wisdom. There can be no advancing or delaying it. That hour cannot come before its time, except as Allah wills, even if the whole of creation demands it or a large group of heedless people keeps mocking this belief.

The beliefs of the polytheists of Arabia (mushrikin) were full of confusion. They did not deny the existence of Allah. Nor did they deny that Allah is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, that He manages the heavens, and that He alone holds up the earth and the heavens. Yet despite this, they associated other deities with Allah. Their view was that they worship these other deities because those deities bring them closer to Allah. Furthermore, they attributed daughters to Allah, although Allah is free from what these people ascribe to Him.

Here Allah mentions their accepted beliefs and holds them to account, so that the confusion present in their beliefs may be removed, and they may be brought to the belief in Tawhid (oneness of Allah), to which their own accepted beliefs also guide them, provided they remain upon their natural disposition (fitrah) and do not deviate.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb, *Fi Zilal al-Quran* (Urdu translation), on Surah al-Mu'minun (23), verses 84–89:**

﴿قُل لِّمَنِ تَسْحَرُونَ﴾ (Verses 84–89)

The confusion in their beliefs was not based on any rational proof, nor did it follow from any logic. This shows how far the beliefs and thoughts of the polytheists in the Arabian Peninsula had deteriorated, even though they claimed to be upon the religion of Ibrahim (Abraham, ﷺ).

﴿قُل لِّمَنِ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ (23:84): "Say: If you know, to whom belong the earth and everyone who inhabits it?" That is, who is the owner of the earth, and who is the owner of the population within it?

﴿سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ﴾ (23:85): "They will surely say, 'Allah is the Owner.'" But in their conduct they do not keep this reality in view, and still they worship other than Allah. Therefore, say to them:

﴿قُلْ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ (23:85): "Will you not then take heed?" Why do you not bring this reality into your conduct?

﴿قُل مَن رَّبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ السَّبْعِ وَرَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ﴾ (23:86): "Ask them: Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Mighty Throne?" This question concerns the lordship (ruboobiyyah, the sole sovereign authority over the cosmos) of this universe: who controls the heavens and the Mighty Throne? The "seven heavens" may mean seven spheres, or groups of seven stars, or seven heavens, or seven worlds, or seven celestial creations. The essential point is the question of who is the controller and the holder of supreme authority over the seven heavens and the Mighty Throne.

﴿سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ﴾ (23:80 as given in the source): "They will surely say, 'Allah.'" But despite this acknowledgment, these people do not fear the Lord of the Mighty Throne, nor do they fear the Lord of the heavens. Rather, they associate others with Him, namely idols that have fallen to the ground.

﴿قُلْ أَفَلَا تَتَّقُونَ﴾ (23:87): "Then why do you not fear Allah?"

﴿قُل مَن بِيَدِهِ مَلَكُوتُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُوَ يُجِيرُ وَلَا يُجَارُ عَلَيْهِ﴾ (23:88): "Say: Tell me, if you know, in whose hand is the sovereignty over everything, and who gives protection while no one can give protection against Him?" This question concerns possession, supreme authority, and kingship: who is the supreme authority? Who is the owner of all things, and over whom does He hold power and control? Who can grant protection to anyone, while no one can give protection against Him? When He grants protection to someone, no one can lay a hand on that person, and when He wishes to seize someone, there is no one who can save the one whom Allah seizes.

﴿سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ﴾ (23:89): "They will surely say, 'It is Allah.'" If you accept these facts, then why are you turning away from the path of guidance? What justification is there for this misguidance?

﴿فَأَنَّىٰ تُسْحَرُونَ﴾ (23:89): "Then from where are you being deluded?" Although, if you know the facts mentioned above, you should not be deluded. The reality is that their beliefs are full of confusion, and these people are afflicted with madness.

Now the appropriate time has come to refute their polytheistic beliefs, to deny that Allah has any offspring, and to pronounce the decision that the true beliefs are those presented by Muhammad (ﷺ).

The confusion in their beliefs was not based on any rational proof, nor did it follow from any logic. This shows how far the beliefs and thoughts of the polytheists in the Arabian Peninsula had deteriorated, even though they claimed to be upon the religion of Ibrahim (Abraham, ﷺ).

﴿قُل لِّمَنِ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ (23:84): "Say: If you know, to whom belong the earth and everyone who inhabits it?" That is, who is the owner of the earth, and who is the owner of the population within it?

﴿سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ﴾ (23:85): "They will surely say, 'Allah is the Owner.'" But in their conduct they do not keep this reality in view, and still they worship other than Allah. Therefore, say to them:

﴿قُلْ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ (23:85): "Will you not then take heed?" Why do you not bring this reality into your conduct?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 23, verses 90–92:

Bal ataynahum bi'l-haqq (Verses 90–92): This judgment comes in various styles. With these people the debate is concluded, and the decision is made that they are liars.

Bal ataynahum bi'l-haqq wa innahum la-kadhibun (23:90): "Rather, We have brought them the truth, and there is no doubt that these people are liars." After this, the detail of their lying is given.

Ma ittakhadha Allahu min waladin (23:91): "Allah has not taken any son, and there is no other god along with Him." And after this, in the course of their claim, the argument is given that there is such weakness in their belief in shirk.

Idhan ladhahaba kullu ilahin bi-ma khalaq (23:91): "Then each god would have taken away what he created." Each god would be an independent deity in his creation, and would act within his creation according to his own specific law of nature. Thus different universes would show different laws, and these would appear as the laws of another god, and the laws of one god would appear separate from the laws of another god. Then, in the case of conflict...

Wa la'ala ba'duhum ala ba'd (23:91): "Then they would overpower one another." In the case of conflict, some gods would dominate others. Thus, in the end, only one god would remain the supreme disposer and sovereign, and in the world only one system would ultimately run, because two sovereigns cannot exist in one country.

Since there is no such conflict in the universe, its unity of structure, the harmony of its movement, and the unity of its order and law of nature are the proof that its sovereign is one, because no clash is seen within the universe or among its parts. It runs in complete harmony, so its Lord and Disposer is also one.

Subhana Allahi 'amma yasifun (23:91): "Glory be to Allah above what they describe." He is the Knower of the unseen and the seen. He has no creation of anyone else, so Allah is free from the shirk that these people propose.

Now the address turns to the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). He is commanded to seek refuge with Allah from being joined with such people, even though Allah has decided what punishment these people will receive, which Allah will show you. In any case, you should seek refuge from the whisperings of Satan, and be patient over what these people say.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 23, verse 93–98:

Qul rabbi immā yurainnahum (Verses 92 to 98)

When these people are given the punishment with which they are being threatened, it is obvious that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) will be saved from it. Yet he is still commanded to keep asking for protection, so that he may safeguard himself further. This is also a kind of teaching for the believers who come after him, so that they do not sit back feeling secure against Allah's punishment and the stratagems of Satan. They should remain alert at all times and keep seeking refuge in Allah.

It is said that Allah has the power to bring the punishment upon them during the lifetime of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Wa innā ʿalā an nuriyaka mā naʿiduhum laqādirūn (23:95) "And indeed We are able to show you what We threaten them with." Allah showed the Prophet (ﷺ) a glimpse of this at the Battle of Badr. After that, a further aspect was shown at the Conquest of Makkah.

Idfaʿ billatī hiya aḥsan al-sayyiʾah naḥnu aʿlamu bimā yaṣifūn (23:96) "O Prophet, repel evil with that which is best; We know well what they attribute to you." At the time this surah was revealed, in Makkah, the method adopted for the call to Islam was to repel evil with good, to be patient until Allah's command arrives, and to leave matters to Allah.

The Prophet's (ﷺ) supplication, "O Lord, I seek refuge in You from the incitements of the devils," was made although he was under Allah's protection and was sinless. This is for greater caution and greater piety, for more earnest supplication to Allah, and for the sake of teaching the Ummah, since the Messenger himself is the model for his Ummah. In reality, this is a teaching for the Ummah that they should always seek Allah's protection from the incitements and whisperings of Satan. Rather, the Messenger (ﷺ) is directed to seek refuge from Satan's approach. Thus it is said:

Wa aʿūdhu bika rabbi an yaḥḍurūn (23:98) "Indeed, I seek refuge in You, O Lord, from their presence (approaching) me." It is also possible that at the time of death the Messenger (ﷺ) sought refuge from Satan appearing at that moment. The next verse, which is in the next lesson, also points to this.

Ḥattā idhā jāʾa aḥadahumu al-mawt (23:99) "Until, when death comes to one of them." This is the style of the Qur'an, in which one meaning flows harmoniously into another.

Ḥattā idhā ... yubʿathūn (23:99–100) "(These people will not give up their deeds) until, when death comes to one of them, he will say, 'My Lord, send me back, that I may do righteousness in what I have left behind.' Never! It is only a word he is saying. Behind them is a barrier (barzakh) until the Day they are resurrected."

In this final lesson too, the discussion of the evil end of the polytheists continues. Now these people are within one of the scenes of the Day of Resurrection. It begins from the time of the taking of souls at the beginning of the world and ends with the blowing of the Trumpet. At the end of the surah, returning to the main theme, they are warned not to call upon anyone else alongside Allah, for there is no deity but Allah. The surah concludes with the guidance that the Messenger (ﷺ) himself should seek forgiveness from Allah.
